“Before joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure are issued, that is called the…” — The Doctrine of the Mean (The Doctrine of the Mean)

Verified English quotation. Primary source: The Doctrine of the Mean. Theme: order.

Quotes / The Doctrine of the Mean / Q0292

English

Before joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure are issued, that is called the Mean; when issued and all hit due measure, that is called Harmony.

School Confucianism

About The Doctrine of the Mean

Biographical certainty varies by figure and text; where the “author” is a scripture or school anthology, read the name as a traditional attribution rather than a modern individual biography.

How to read this passage

Philosophers ask whether order is discovered in nature, imposed by rulers, or cultivated through custom. Chaos and creativity stand as its counterparts. This passage enters that discussion through order, desire.

Concepts in this quote

Order
Order names cosmos, ritual, law, and the patterned stability that makes shared life possible—or oppressive.
Desire
Desire drives action and suffering alike; philosophy asks which desires to educate, restrain, or affirm.
